review_notes: I read the whole file and the definitions it depends on: SourceLabeledLattice, referenceLabels, referenceFamily, sum_reference_frozen, physicalMainScale, physicalCenteredMaskedBand, physicalFrozenCenteredCoefficient. I also checked the downstream use of the narrow-reference theorems in SourceLabeledNarrowTail.lean. The Type-level universe restrictions (κ, Label, Item : Type) come from the structure definition, so they are not a local defect. The restriction to oldSlope = newSlope = t is the intended 'Self' design, and I did not treat it as a defect. The only finding is that the per-scale theorems assume short and support conditions for every scale j although their conclusions concern a single j. I did not compile the proposed change. The Square proof would need a small adjustment because `simp_rw` must supply the per-j hypotheses.

findings.excerpt: (hshort : ∀ j l k, b j l k t ≠ 0 → P.length j ≤ R)
findings.problem: The conclusion concerns one fixed scale `j`, because `physicalMainScale ... j y x` is a sum over `l` and `u` at that `j` only. The hypotheses `hshort` and `hsupport` are quantified over all scales `j`, and the target `j` is bound after them. The proof applies `sum_reference_frozen` at that single `j`, whose own hypotheses `hshort`/`hsupport` only mention `l u k` at that `j`. So the statement is stronger than needed. A caller who knows the short/cone conditions at one scale cannot use the theorem. The same pattern occurs in `physicalCenteredMaskedBand_eq_narrow_reference`, around lines 141–143.
findings.proposed_change: Move `(j : Fin N)` before the hypotheses and weaken them to `(hshort : ∀ l k, b j l k t ≠ 0 → P.length j ≤ R)` and `(hsupport : ∀ l k, b j l k t ≠ 0 → |t+P.rowSlope j l-t| ≤ cone*w/P.length j)`. Apply the same change to `physicalCenteredMaskedBand_eq_narrow_reference`. The proof body is unchanged except that `hshort j l k hk` becomes `hshort l k hk`. The all-scales versions follow by specialising, so `physicalMainSquare_eq_narrow_reference` and `physicalCenteredMaskedVariation_eq_narrow_reference` keep their `∀ j` hypotheses. Their calls become `fun j => ... (hshort j) (hsupport j)`. In the Square proof, `simp_rw` will need to be replaced by `funext`/`Finset.sum_congr` or by an explicit `have` over `j`.
findings.benefit: The per-scale restriction lemmas become usable when the packet-length and cone conditions are only known, or only true, at some scales. The hypotheses then match what the proof uses. Existing all-scale callers, such as the use in SourceLabeledNarrowTail.lean, need only a trivial adjustment.
